items.title: Section: Restraint at Two Depths — Suppressing Affliction Versus Uprooting It for Good

items.zh: 謂由正念，防護於意，行平等位，是名正防護。又略義者，謂若防護方便、若所防護事、若正防護。如是一切總略為一，名根律儀。此中云何防護方便？謂防守正念，常委正念。眼見色已，不取其相，不取隨好；廣說乃至意知法已，不取其相，不取隨好。若依是處發生種種惡不善法，令心流漏，即於是處修行律儀。防守根故，名修律儀。如是名為防護方便。云何名為所防護事？所謂眼色，乃至意法。如是名為所防護事。此中云何名正防護？謂如說言：由其正念，防護於意，行平等位。名正防護。又根律儀略有二種。一者、思擇力所攝，二者、修習力所攝。思擇力所攝根律儀者，謂於境界深見過患，不能於此所有過患除遣斷滅。修習力所攝根律儀者，謂於境界深見過患，亦能於此所有過患除遣斷滅。又由思擇力所攝根律儀故，於所緣境，令煩惱纏不復生起、不復現前；而於依附所依隨眠，不能斷除、不能永拔。由修習力所攝根律儀故，於所緣境，煩惱隨眠不復生起、不復現前；一切時分，依附所依所有隨眠，亦能斷除、亦能永拔。
items.en: It is through correct mindfulness protecting the mind, resting in equanimity — this is called correct protection. …Restraint of the faculties, in brief, is of two kinds: that comprised within the power of discernment, and that comprised within the power of cultivation. Restraint of the faculties comprised within the power of discernment means that, seeing deeply the faults inherent in objects, one is nonetheless unable to remove and eliminate all such faults entirely. Restraint of the faculties comprised within the power of cultivation means that, seeing deeply the faults inherent in objects, one is also able to remove and eliminate all such faults entirely. …Through restraint of the faculties comprised within the power of discernment, with regard to a given object, the entanglements of affliction [their active manifestation] no longer arise, no longer manifest — yet the underlying tendencies, resting on their own basis, cannot be cut off, cannot be permanently uprooted. Through restraint of the faculties comprised within the power of cultivation, with regard to a given object, the underlying tendencies of affliction no longer arise, no longer manifest — and, at all times, the underlying tendencies resting on their own basis are also cut off, also permanently uprooted.

items.zh: 如是思擇力所攝根律儀、修習力所攝根律儀，有此差別，有此意趣，有此殊異。

items.title: Section: Restraint of the Faculties Closes — Moderation in Eating Opens

items.zh: 當知此中思擇力所攝根律儀，是資糧道所攝；修習力所攝根律儀，當知墮在離欲地攝。云何名為於食知量？謂如有一，由正思擇食於所食。不為倡蕩、不為憍逸、不為飾好、不為端嚴，乃至廣說。
items.en: It should be understood that restraint of the faculties comprised within the power of discernment belongs to the path of provisions; restraint of the faculties comprised within the power of cultivation should be understood as belonging to the ground of detachment. …What is called moderation in eating? It is that one, through correct discernment, eats what is eaten — not for wanton pleasure, not for pride and indulgence, not to enhance one's beauty, not for physical elegance — and so on at length, as already stated.

items.zh: 云何名為由正思擇食於所食？

items.title: Contemplating Food's Faults: From Appetizing to Repulsive in Three Swallows

items.zh: 正思擇者，如以妙慧等隨觀察段食過患。見過患已，深生厭惡，然後吞咽。云何名為觀見過患？謂即於此所食段食，或觀受用種類過患、或觀變異種類過患、或觀追求種類過患。云何受用種類過患？謂如有一，將欲食時，所受段食色香味觸皆悉圓滿，甚為精妙。從此無間進至口中，牙齒咀嚼，津唾浸爛，涎液纏裹，轉入咽喉。爾時此食先曾所有悅意妙相一切皆捨，次後轉成可惡穢相，當轉異時，狀如變吐。能食士夫補特伽羅，若正思念此位穢相，於餘未變一切精妙所受飲食，初尚不能住食欣樂，況於此位。由如是等非一相貌漸次受用增上力故，令其飲食淨妙相沒，過患相生，不淨所攝。是名於食受用種類所有過患。云何轉變種類過患？謂此飲食既噉食已，一分消變，至中夜分或後夜分，於其身中，便能生起養育增長血肉筋脈骨髓皮等非一眾多種種品類諸不淨物。次後一分變成便穢，變已趣下展轉流出。
items.en: Correct discernment means observing, with excellent wisdom, either the full range or some part of the faults inherent in solid food. Having seen these faults, one gives rise to deep revulsion, and only then swallows. …With regard to this very food being eaten, one observes the faults of its consumption, or the faults of its transformation, or the faults of the pursuit required to obtain it. …It is like one who, about to eat, finds the food received — its colour, aroma, taste, and texture — entirely complete, truly excellent and refined. Yet the moment it enters the mouth, chewed by the teeth, soaked and softened by saliva, wrapped in mucus, and passed down into the throat, every one of its previously delightful, excellent qualities is entirely abandoned, transforming instead into something repulsive and filthy — becoming, at the moment of this transformation, like excrement. …This food, once eaten, is in part transformed: by the middle or the last watch of the night, within the body, it gives rise to and nourishes blood, flesh, sinew, marrow, bone, skin, and many other kinds of impure substances. Another part is transformed into excrement, which then passes downwards and is expelled.

blocks.text: Restraint of the senses closes; moderation in eating opens. The treatise's account of food is frank, even graphic: it is meant to loosen attachment to taste.

Restraint by **the power of discernment**: one sees the faults of objects but cannot yet remove the latent tendencies; affliction is held back but can still arise. Master Cháng Bǎi: an underlying tendency is affliction's seed; given conditions, it will surface. Restraint by **the power of cultivation**: one who has at least access concentration and practises calm and insight. Then "the latent tendencies resting on their own basis are permanently uprooted". Venerable Miào Jìng: the basis is the ālayavijñāna.
"Through correct discernment, one eats not for pleasure, not for pride." Master Cháng Bǎi: every matter of daily life is part of practice.

"Correct discernment means observing, with excellent wisdom, either the full range or some part of the faults of solid food": the faults of **consumption**, of **transformation**, of the **pursuit** needed to obtain it.

Consumption: fine food, chewed and mixed with saliva, quickly becomes repulsive "in three swallows". Transformation: in the night it is digested into waste. Venerable Miào Jìng: for some in the middle watch, for some in the last. Master Cháng Bǎi: this "does not mean refusing to eat, but not clinging".

quiz.q: What can restraint comprised within the power of discernment do, and what can it not do?
options: it sees the faults of objects deeply but cannot remove and eliminate them
it sees no faults at all
quiz.why: "Restraint of the faculties comprised within the power of discernment means that, seeing deeply the faults inherent in objects, one is nonetheless unable to remove and eliminate all such faults entirely." Master Cháng Bǎi: discernment cannot yet cut the seeds of affliction, so the faults are not fully removed.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain "underlying tendencies"?
options: a latent potential of affliction — its seed — which will still surface when conditions meet
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: an underlying tendency is a latent potential of affliction, its seed; given conditions it will still surface. So discernment can stop the active fetters but cannot uproot the tendencies.

quiz.q: Restraint by the power of cultivation belongs to the ground of detachment. How do the masters differ on the level this requires?
options: both say an ordinary distracted mind
Cháng Bǎi: at least access concentration; Miào Jìng: detachment lies beyond access concentration, in form-realm absorption
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the power of cultivation belongs to one who has at least access concentration and practises calm and insight within it. Venerable Miào Jìng: the ground of detachment lies beyond desire-realm and access concentration, in form-realm absorption.

quiz.q: Opening the topic of moderation in eating, how does Master Cháng Bǎi regard eating?
options: eating has nothing to do with practice
everything in daily life is practice, and so is eating
practitioners should not eat at all
the more one eats, the better one practices
quiz.why: "It is that one, through correct discernment, eats what is eaten — not for wanton pleasure, not for pride and indulgence." Master Cháng Bǎi: every matter of daily life is practice, and eating too is practice.

quiz.q: The text says to give rise to deep revulsion and only then swallow. What does Master Cháng Bǎi say "deep revulsion" means?
options: not refusing to eat, but not craving it
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: it does not mean refusing to eat, but not clinging; deep revulsion means not craving.

quiz.q: Into which three kinds does the treatise divide the faults of solid food?
options: the faults of consumption, of transformation, and of pursuit
faults of colour, aroma, and taste
quiz.why: "One observes the faults of its consumption, or the faults of its transformation, or the faults of the pursuit required to obtain it." Master Cháng Bǎi: observing all three is "full" observation; observing one or two is "partial."

quiz.q: The English renders 狀如變吐 as "indistinguishable from vomit." How does Venerable Miào Jìng read 變吐?
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: what does 變吐 mean? It means excretion — the food becomes just like that. The English takes it as vomit; the lecture takes it as excrement.
